tfn.s: The city council has limited balcony rental prices.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not mention any city council rules on balcony prices.

tfn.s: Nobody can watch the processions without paying.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "people can still watch many processions from the public streets without paying anything."

tfn.s: The quoted prices cover the whole week, not a single procession.

tfn.s: The writer implies that the high price of a balcony reflects competition for places rather than a better view.
tfn.why: The text says "The balcony itself has not improved; the number of people competing for it has risen."

speak.title: Role-play: who gets the balcony?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: A travel company wants to rent your balcony for Holy Week at a very high price. A neighbour's family has watched from it for years. Listen to the neighbour, then decide: sell it to the company, keep it for the family, or find a compromise.

b.text: Your family has always watched the processions from your neighbour's balcony. Ask to use it again this year. Explain why it matters to you and offer something in return.

phrases: I was hoping to ask you a favour.
I'd love to say yes, but it's a lot of money.
What if we shared the week?
I'm afraid I can't do that.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: who got the balcony, and was it a fair decision?
